study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Lin et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used quantile polynomial regression to build the normative model. The model estimated 5th, 50th (median), and 95th percentiles with bootstrapping confidence intervals based on second-order polynomial regression. A 10-fold cross-validation was used to build an aggregation normative model. The authors also validated the results using a quantile linear regression model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A quantile polynomial regression model was used to determine percentile curves based on the second-order polynomial regression (Koenker, 2005; Lv et al., 2020). Compared to conventional regression seeking the mean of the variable to be predicted, quantile regression aims to seek the median or any other percentiles. ... In this study, we specifically estimated the 5th, 50th (median), and 95th percentiles with bootstrapping confidence intervals to obtain the normative distribution separately.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled dynamic functional connectivity (FC-dynamic characteristics) and network fluctuation characteristics derived from resting-state fMRI. Dynamic functional connectivity matrices were computed using a sliding-time window method (window length = 60s) based on 90 ROIs from the AAL atlas. Subject-specific inherent connectivity networks and time-varying weight variability were computed using group information-guided independent component analysis (GIG-ICA) with 20 independent components.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For each subject, we computed whole-brain time-varying connectivity matrices based on m (m = 90) ROIs from the automated anatomical labeling (AAL) template (Tzourio-Mazoyer et al., 2002) using a sliding time window method (window length = 60s) (Allen et al., 2014; Du et al., 2017) as dynamic functional connectivity patterns. ... Then, the FC-dynamic (dynamic of functional connectivity) characteristics and network fluctuation characteristics were calculated based on these connectivity networks.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Lin2023.pdf.md: Section 2.2 Individual-level dynamic functional connectivity patterns

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model was fitted using age (modified as physical age minus average age of the healthy-base group), quadratic age term (age^2 as part of second-order polynomial), and sex as explanatory variables. The regression equation included these covariates to predict each dynamic characteristic (Ci).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: For the healthy-base participant with index i, sexi encodes the participant's sex (male: 0, female: 1), agei is the modified age of the participant (physical age minus the average age of the healthy-base group). β is a set of parameters that control the scale of the regression function used to interpolate the data and the relevance of each covariate for predicting the response Ci.
